course.title: React Native: build, reconnect, restore and release the Craves app
course.description: Follow the real apps/mobile implementation from TypeScript contracts to navigation, secure sessions, cart reconciliation and Android/iOS delivery. Includes local exercises, failure matrices and the manual signing boundaries.

lessons.title: Understand the mobile workspace and trace a user action
lessons.overview: React Native renders a mobile application, while the Spring services remain the owners of Craves business state. The working mobile source is apps/mobile. Its package.json contains the actual commands and dependency baseline; this course does not silently upgrade React Native or replace the project with a new Expo application. Metro supplies JavaScript during development, native Android/iOS projects build installable applications, and TypeScript describes contracts that still require runtime validation at external boundaries. A screen that works with a fixture is not proof that the production API route, identity and state model agree.

steps.label: Establish a clean baseline
steps.detail: From the repository root record git rev-parse HEAD, then enter apps/mobile and inspect package.json and its lockfile. Run npm ci rather than resolving an unrelated set of latest versions. Use the Node range declared by this source revision. Record install and test errors instead of changing dependencies until the app happens to start.

steps.label: Read the actual commands
steps.detail: The workspace defines start, android, ios, lint, test, test:integration and test:e2e. npm run start starts Metro; it does not deploy Azure or submit to an app store. npm run android and npm run ios invoke the native development tooling. The test:e2e script currently invokes Jest tests; its name is not evidence of a physical-device or store-distribution test.

steps.label: Map one feature boundary
steps.detail: Locate a feature's screen, domain types, API adapter and state logic rather than putting all four responsibilities in a component. For cart actions, follow cartMutations.ts into cartApi and the accepted CartSnapshot. Write down where a pending action is represented, where an error is normalized and where an authoritative response replaces local state.

steps.label: Trace the shared HTTP client
steps.detail: httpClient.ts separates read and write methods. Reads can use a dedupeKey through runDedupedRequest; writes record sanitized mutation events and use the configured API client. A TypeScript generic on an HTTP response is not a runtime schema check. Locate the actual feature parser before assuming an arbitrary server object satisfies its type.

steps.label: Separate visual and business state
steps.detail: A selected tab, animation and expanded section can be local UI state. Ownership, availability, payable totals and order progression are backend facts. A new screen should present loading, denied, empty, failed and successful states without making up a success value when an API is unavailable.

steps.label: Reproduce before extending
steps.detail: Run the focused existing tests for the feature before editing. Then document the request path, source API, parser, reducer or query state, navigation destination and rendered component. This map is the starting point for an approved feature, not a license to duplicate pricing or authentication inside the app.

lessons.example: Tapping Add can create a pending mobile mutation and temporarily disable duplicate taps. The returned server cart snapshot establishes accepted state. A spinner disappearing alone does not establish that the server accepted the command.
lessons.lab: Create a local trace worksheet for one cart action. Run npm test -- --runInBand src/features/cart/cartMutations.test.ts using the path from the workspace's integration script, then confirm the reported tests actually ran. Trace the production implementation at src/features/cart/state/cartMutations.ts and identify its API and state dependencies. Record any difference between the test file's location and the implementation's location. Build a screen-state table for loading, pending, applied, duplicate-suppressed, failed and stale-session cases. Do not connect the exercise to real payments or delivery bookings.
lessons.pitfall: Do not confuse a JavaScript test suite named e2e with a real Android/iOS end-to-end journey. Report simulator, device, mocked and live evidence separately.

questions.prompt: What does Metro do in the mobile development workflow?
questions.explanation: Metro is the JavaScript development bundler, not the backend or store deployment system.

questions.prompt: A response is typed as CartSnapshot in TypeScript. Is the received JSON automatically validated?
options: No; runtime validation must occur at the boundary
questions.explanation: Compile-time types do not validate network bytes at runtime.

questions.prompt: The test:e2e command runs Jest. What can its name alone prove?
options: Nothing about real-device coverage without examining the tests
questions.explanation: Evidence must describe what the tests actually execute, not infer coverage from their name.

lessons.title: Handle token refresh, temporary outages and role changes safely
lessons.overview: Mobile applications frequently lose connectivity, sleep in the background and restart after the operating system kills their process. Those are normal lifecycle events, not automatic reasons to delete a user's session. Craves sessionManager separates an in-memory access token from a persisted refresh session, coalesces concurrent refreshes and distinguishes terminal credential rejection from transient service failures. Learn the actual behavior before changing it. Customer and chef mobile sessions are not the same administrative session policy used by the internal web portal, even when the same person has multiple roles.

steps.label: Trace credential ownership
steps.detail: sessionManager.ts imports tokenMemory and refreshTokenStore. Read their concrete storage adapters before documenting platform storage guarantees. Never copy tokens into a screen, debug console, analytics property, navigation parameter or training fixture. A long-lived refresh credential is not ordinary preference data.

steps.label: Understand single-flight refresh
steps.detail: The shared refreshPromise means concurrent callers await one refresh operation, and finally clears the promise for the next attempt. This coordinates callers in one running JavaScript process. It is not a server-side idempotency guarantee and does not synchronize two different devices.

steps.label: Classify failures
steps.detail: The implementation invalidates missing, expired or rejected credentials and handles a persistence failure as a terminal problem. On a transient network/service error it preserves the persisted refresh credential and rethrows a normalized error so a later retry can recover. Show a reconnect state rather than pretending the user is authenticated and the operation succeeded.

steps.label: Persist before publishing access
steps.detail: The refresh path saves the rotated refresh token before installing the new access token in memory. If persistence fails, the service invalidates credentials rather than leaving a partially established session. Test this failure deliberately with a storage mock instead of assuming secure storage always succeeds.

steps.label: Clear user-specific state
steps.detail: A logout or role switch must not leave another role's order, address or profile cache visible. Follow the existing role-switch and invalidation tests referenced by test:integration. A successful refresh must not restore data after the user has deliberately signed out; check request generation and cancellation behavior in the relevant caller.

steps.label: Separate retry categories
steps.detail: A safe read can usually be reissued after the session is restored according to the client contract. An uncertain checkout, payment or booking write needs its own receipt/status reconciliation. Do not attach a blanket retry policy to every HTTP method because the refresh code now works.

lessons.example: Several screens request data after the app resumes. They should share refresh work rather than rotate the same credential independently. If the network times out, preserve the recoverable session but do not mark an unknown payment as paid or automatically create a replacement order.
lessons.lab: Run npm test -- --runInBand src/features/auth/api/sessionManager.test.ts from apps/mobile. Add local test cases for concurrent refresh callers, transient timeout, rejected refresh, expired stored session and failure to save the rotated token. For each case, assert token-memory state, persisted credential behavior, invalidation notifications and API call count. Then simulate switching from chef to customer while a chef-data request is delayed. Confirm that stale data cannot populate the customer view. Record mocked versus device-tested behavior explicitly.
lessons.pitfall: A local request queue or shared promise is not proof of exactly-once server execution. Durable side effects require server-side protection and reconciliation.

questions.prompt: What is the intended response to a transient refresh network failure?
options: Preserve the recoverable credential and expose a retryable failure
questions.explanation: Transient connectivity failures differ from terminal credential rejection.

options: Refresh callers in this running JavaScript process
questions.explanation: It is an in-process single-flight mechanism, not a global distributed lock.

questions.prompt: Why must failure to persist a rotated refresh token be tested?
options: It can otherwise leave inconsistent credential state
questions.explanation: The implementation must not publish a partially established session after secure persistence fails.

lessons.title: Build safe deep links, process restoration and a feature state machine
lessons.overview: Navigation is an input boundary. A link or saved route can be malformed, stale or inappropriate for the currently authorized role. Craves inboundRouting.ts parses supported craves:// destinations, checks readiness and role context, and returns NAVIGATE, DEFER or BLOCKED. processRestoration.ts stores a versioned allowlisted route snapshot rather than serializing the whole screen tree and all user form data. These controls preserve user experience without treating navigation as authorization. The backend must still verify that a requested order or kitchen resource may be read.

steps.label: Read the parser contract
steps.detail: The pinned parser accepts specific canonical destinations and validates resource identifiers. It rejects extra query or fragment syntax rather than interpreting arbitrary routes. Follow parseInboundUrl before extending any link format. Any new supported destination needs an explicit parsing rule and tests for malformed or overlong input.

steps.label: Respect readiness states
steps.detail: resolveInboundRoute defers when authentication or product initialization is incomplete. Once the role is known, an order destination resolves to the appropriate customer or chef detail view. Do not navigate to protected content first and validate the user afterward; that can flash stale or unauthorized data.

steps.label: Preserve unavailable features
steps.detail: At this source snapshot, the recognized offer destination deliberately returns DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE because its authoritative eligibility contract is not available. Do not invent a functional offers screen or business rule to make every deep link appear supported. Document the gap as a product dependency.

steps.label: Restore only reviewed context
steps.detail: processRestoration.ts validates a versioned snapshot using strict schemas and an allowlist of customer and chef destinations. Draft-bearing forms are excluded or fall back to a safe owning tab. A resource ID may be saved as navigation context, but the actual resource must be fetched and authorized again after restart.

steps.label: Handle repeated events
steps.detail: Inbound events may arrive through multiple lifecycle hooks. createInboundRouteDedupe suppresses repeated navigation inside its bounded local window. This is a UX guard, not a durable authorization or payment receipt. Reset its state where the lifecycle requires it and test release/retry behavior when navigation itself fails.

steps.label: Design the complete feature journey
steps.detail: For an approved new feature, define entry by tab, notification and deep link; loading and permission states; edit/mutation outcome; back behavior; role switch; offline resume; and process death. Update navigation types and parsers together. Keep an unavailable backend capability visibly unavailable rather than restoring a fictional successful state.

lessons.example: A saved customer order-detail route can restore its order ID after the process restarts, but the application must authenticate again and request the current authorized order view. It must not restore a previously cached paid badge as proof of payment.
lessons.lab: Run the existing inboundRouting.test.ts and processRestoration.test.ts with npm test -- --runInBand followed by both paths. Produce a matrix covering malformed link, signed-out link, product-not-ready, wrong role, duplicate event, unavailable offer destination, old snapshot version and draft-bearing form. Then test a real simulator restart using synthetic data: navigate to a resource, background and terminate the process, relaunch and confirm reauthorization plus a fresh read. Jest success alone does not establish operating-system restoration behavior.
lessons.pitfall: Persisting the full navigation state can unintentionally persist sensitive drafts or stale domain facts. A safe restore target is not a saved business transaction.

questions.prompt: A deep link arrives before authentication is ready. What is the appropriate route outcome?
options: Defer until the required context is verified
questions.explanation: Protected navigation must wait for verified identity and product readiness.

questions.prompt: What does restoring a saved order ID authorize?
options: Only navigation context; the backend must reauthorize the resource
questions.explanation: Resource identifiers do not establish ownership or authorization.

questions.prompt: Why is the offer link blocked in this reviewed source?
options: The authoritative destination/eligibility capability is not available
questions.explanation: The implementation intentionally fails closed rather than inventing an unsupported feature.

lessons.title: Validate the complete app and prepare a controlled Android/iOS release
lessons.overview: A mobile release combines source, native builds, signing, backend compatibility and device behavior. It cannot be accepted solely because TypeScript compiles or a debug simulator opens the home screen. Use the existing scripts and native project configuration, keep signing material outside source control, and record the exact tested artifact. This course does not create store accounts, change signing keys or publish an app. Those are separate authorized console actions. The capstone is an evidence-backed feature handover covering both customer and chef journeys, interrupted connectivity and accessibility.

steps.label: Run the source gates
steps.detail: Use npm ci, npm run lint, npm test -- --runInBand and the checked-in integration script as appropriate. Inspect each script before claiming coverage. Capture the source SHA, package-lock baseline, test reports and known skips. Do not bypass failing tests with a different lockfile or by excluding the failing feature.

steps.label: Exercise device lifecycle
steps.detail: Test cold start, foreground resume, offline start, loss of connectivity during a read, an uncertain mutation, process termination and role switch. Include a small-screen device and text-size changes. Confirm focus labels, touch targets, keyboard behavior and reduced-motion handling. Clearly separate mocked, simulator and physical-device results.

steps.label: Measure meaningful performance
steps.detail: Observe initial render, list scrolling, image memory, screen transitions and repeated navigation. Bound subscriptions, polling and pending requests; clean them up when screens unmount or roles change. A smooth single test device does not establish backend throughput, and one server replica is not proof of million-user capacity.

steps.label: Protect native configuration
steps.detail: Use the existing Firebase and API environment configuration for the intended test target. Do not paste service-account keys or provider secrets into mobile .env files; a distributed application cannot keep backend secrets confidential. Review compiled configuration and observability redaction as part of the release, not after a store upload.

steps.label: Record manual store boundaries
steps.detail: Android release signing and Play Console access, and Apple Developer enrollment, certificates, provisioning and App Store Connect access, remain owner-controlled actions. Work from the current native Gradle/Xcode configuration and approved signing setup. Never replace a working signing key to simplify an exercise. Current store requirements must be verified during the actual release.

steps.label: Plan compatibility and recovery
steps.detail: Older installed clients can continue calling APIs after a new version is released. Prefer additive contracts, meaningful capability handling and backend-compatible rollback. Record the build identifier and distribution track, verify the installable artifact, and define how to halt rollout or disable a faulty capability without deleting user data.

lessons.example: A new optional response field should not cause an older installed app to crash. A new mobile screen should also handle a backend where its capability is not enabled yet. Both combinations belong in the release matrix.
lessons.lab: Prepare a release packet for one local training feature: exact changed paths, API dependency, focused tests, integration tests, simulator/device matrix, sanitized performance observations, artifact identifier, signing owner, distribution target and rollback plan. Include customer and chef role-switch results and an interrupted-write reconciliation case. A peer must reproduce the feature from a clean checkout and explain its unsupported states. Mark store publication, real provider interaction and production acceptance NOT EXECUTED unless independently authorized and actually observed.
lessons.pitfall: A mobile app's secrets and credentials must not be treated like server-side Key Vault values. Anything shipped in the application should be assessed as inspectable by its recipients.

questions.prompt: Which item must not be embedded in a distributed mobile application?
questions.explanation: Provider secrets belong on the backend and in approved secret stores, not in distributed client code.

questions.prompt: Why must a release consider older installed clients?
options: Installed versions may continue using the backend contract
questions.explanation: Mobile rollout is not instantaneous, so API compatibility must span supported installed versions.

questions.prompt: What should be recorded when store publication has not occurred?
options: Not executed, with the remaining owner-controlled steps
questions.explanation: Build evidence must not be presented as store or production acceptance.
